dedupe_keys.name: demand side solutions in the us building sector scout and gridsim model runs and results

description: This Mendeley Data record holds the model inputs and results behind a study by Jared Langevin and co-authors at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, funded by the US Department of Energy, on decarbonising US buildings together with the power grid. Building efficiency, demand flexibility and electrification measures are assessed with the Scout model against the EIA Annual Energy Outlook 2021 reference case, and annual electricity emission factors and hourly power system costs come from the Brattle GridSIM model under several grid decarbonisation scenarios. The study finds up to a 91% cut in building CO2 emissions from 2005 levels by 2050 and up to $107 billion a year in avoided power system costs from efficiency and flexibility. Files are a workbook with instructions to reproduce the Scout runs, figure and table data workbooks, the Scout measure sets, raw Scout results with GridSIM hourly cost and emissions data, and post-processing data. Coverage: the United States building stock, new and existing, to 2050. Access: XLSX and ZIP files on Mendeley Data, version 1 published 2023-08-18. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: results are projections under stated assumptions and depend on the proprietary GridSIM model, which is not included. Simulation uses are reproducing building demand scenarios for grid capacity planning and testing how building flexibility changes power system stress. Related records: the Scout model record and the End-Use Load Profiles record.
